Gelir dengesi: The situation in which, in a given period, the total quantity demanded and the total quantity supplied in the economy equal each other.
Gelir esnekliği: Or the income elasticity of demand, in short εY: a basic type of elasticity showing by what percentage the quantity demanded of a certain product changes as a result of a one percent increase in consumers' income.
Gelir etkisi: The change seen because of the change in purchasing power when the price of a product or input changes.
Gelir eşdeğerliği kanıtsavı: A mathematical demonstration showing that, under the assumptions of participants being risk-neutral and of the value of the product being private to the individual, the same revenue is obtained on average from the four fundamental auction types.
Gelir Vergisi Stopajı Desteği: The withholding of, at certain rates and for a certain period, the income tax withholding that the employer must pay for additional employment, provided to investments with an investment incentive certificate arranged under the Regional Investment Incentive System.
Gelir-tüketim eğrisi: Or the Engel curve: a graphical tool showing the relationship between the consumer's income and the quantity demanded of a certain good, all else being constant.
Gelire Endeksli Senetler: With the aim of increasing domestic savings, diversifying Government Domestic Debt Securities and broadening the investor base, the first Revenue-Indexed Securities (GES) issue was carried out by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance of the Republic of Türkiye on 28 January 2009. In GES issues, returns are indexed to the revenue shares transferred to the budget from the Türkiye Petrolleri Anonim Ortaklığı (TPAO), which has the status of a State Economic Enterprise, the State Supply Office (DMO), the State Airports Authority (DHMİ) and the General Directorate of Coastal Safety (KIYEM). With Revenue-Indexed Securities, an investment instrument has been created whose return is linked to state revenues. Thanks to the minimum coupon payment guarantee to be applied to the said securities, the investor is protected from being adversely affected by the change in the revenue share. Within this framework, in calculating the payments relating to the returns of the said securities, the total of the quarterly and semi-annual revenue shares transferred to the budget by TPAO, DMO, DHMİ and KIYEM is taken as the basis. If the realized revenue collection exceeds the maximum amounts announced in the budget, payment is made to investors based on the counterparts of the said maximum amounts.
Gelirin yeniden dağıtımı: The practices directed at transferring wealth, directly or indirectly, from high-income segments to low-income segments.
Genel Bütçe: The budget of the public institutions forming the legal personality of the state, such as the Grand National Assembly of Türkiye, the Presidency, the Prime Ministry, the Constitutional Court, the Court of Cassation, the Council of State, the Court of Accounts and the various ministries.
Genel Devlet Dengesi: Consists of the balances of the central government budget, local administrations, social security institutions, general health insurance, funds, revolving funds and the unemployment insurance fund. This definition is taken as the basis in international comparisons.
Genel fiyat düzeyi: Or in short P: the conceptual quantity denoting collectively the prices of all the goods and services in the economy.
Genel Teşvik Uygulamaları: Within the Investment Incentive System, the incentives that investments not falling within the scope of regional, priority or large-scale investments can benefit from, on the condition of meeting the minimum investment amount. Natural Person: the term legally defining the period of a person from the womb until death, on the conditions of being born alive and remaining alive.
Genişleme yolu: Or the output-factor curve: a graphical tool showing how the factor bundles used by the producer change as total product increases, all else being constant.
Genişlemeci açık: Or a positive output gap: the situation in which, in the short run, real GDP is above potential GDP, and hence the economy is considered to be in an expansion period.
Genişletici maliye politikası: Fiscal policy aimed at increasing aggregate demand and real GDP.
Genişletici para politikası: Monetary policy aimed at increasing aggregate demand and real GDP.
Gentlemen’s Agreements: Such agreements, not binding in written form, are defined as tacit cooperatives shaped by the degree of allegiance the participating parties feel toward their provisions, and are examined within the framework of 'agreements, concerted practices and/or decisions' in Article 4 of the Competition Act.
Genç işsizliği oranı: The percentage showing the share of the unemployed young population aged 15-24 within the young labor force in an economy.
Geri Dönüşüm: The inclusion of waste having the possibility of re-evaluation back into the production process, by converting it into a secondary raw material after passing through various physical and/or chemical processes.
Geri Kazanım: The recovery of unusable recyclable waste materials into manufacturing processes again as raw material through various recycling methods. GES: the abbreviation of Solar Power Plant, systems converting the energy coming from the sun into electrical energy. Input: the in-kind and financial resources necessary for the realization of project activities and used in project activities.
Geri ödeme süresi: The period showing in how much time an investment recovers its initial cost with its cash inflows; it is an incomplete method because it ignores time value.
Geri Ödenmeme Riski: Refers to the risk of the debt not being repaid.
Gerçek Zamanlı Brüt Mutabakat: The settlement of fund and securities transfers individually and instantaneously (continuously), in an order, without netting. Although classifiable in various respects, payment systems are classified, according to the settlement type, into real-time gross settlement systems and settlement systems based on netting. Today the great majority of payment systems of systemic importance operate with real-time gross settlement methods.
Getiri Eğrisi / Verim Eğrisi: The graphical expression of the relationship, in any time interval, between the various maturities of an investment instrument and the returns at those maturities. The vertical axis holds return/yield, the horizontal axis the maturities. They are classified as positively sloped (normal) yield curves, negatively sloped (inverted) yield curves, flat yield curves and yield curves expressing high returns at medium maturities (bell shape). The movements of the curve over time — its steepening ('steeping': if a positively sloped curve is in question, the distant part of the curve rising and the near part falling, the slope increasing), its flattening ('flattening': in positively sloped yield curves, the distant part falling, the near part rising, the slope decreasing) and the curve moving up or down without changing its shape ('parallel shift') — are so named. An increase in the curve's slope reflects the expectation that interest rates (inflation) will rise in the long term. A decrease in the slope — in other words, the flattening of a positively sloped yield curve (the near side rising, the distant side falling) — expresses investors, with the expectation that interest rates will fall in the future, turning toward the long term in order to benefit from the current interest rates for longer, and hence, with the increasing demand, the return at that maturity falling; and those demanding funds, with the expectation that the opportunity of borrowing at lower interest rates will arise in the future, preferring the short term, and hence, with the excess supply, the return rising.
Geç Likidite Penceresi: The Late Liquidity Window (GLP) refers to the overnight TL borrowing facility that the CBRT, in its capacity as lender of last resort, provides without limit to banks at the end of the day (between 16:00 and 17:00), against collateral, in order to prevent problems that may arise in the payment systems and to meet their temporary liquidity needs, and the overnight TL lending facility it provides under the same conditions so that liquidity surpluses can be evaluated.
Geçmişe dönük öngörü yanılgısı: The tendency to think 'it was obvious all along' after an event has occurred; it evaluates forecasting success as higher than it is.
Gider minimizasyonu: The selection of the factor bundle that will minimize total cost for a certain quantity of production, with factor prices given.
Giffen malı: A compulsory, fundamental good whose quantity demanded increases rather than decreases as its price rises.
Girdi maliyeti: Or factor cost: the cost of the resources such as labor, capital and land used in the production process.
Girdi piyasası: Or the factor market: the markets where the instruments and materials required for production are bought and sold.
Giriş engeli: Or a barrier to market entry: the natural or artificial restrictions that make it difficult to sell or buy in a certain market.
GSYH deflatörü: A price index taking as its product basket all the goods and services within the scope of GDP.
Gun Jumping: The implementation of a concentration transaction without notification or without permission, including restrictive agreements, exchange of information and unlawful coordination among the parties prior to the transaction.
Gölge Bankacılık: Non-bank credit intermediation activities carrying risks like the banking sector. The shadow banking sector, not subject to regulations as strict as the banking sector's, carries out maturity transformation activities like banks, and is exposed to liquidity risk and risks arising from high leverage.
Göreceli yoksulluk: The state of not having enough income to attain the average living conditions in a country.
Göreceli yoksulluk oranı: The ratio of the population having less income than the average income in a country to the total population.
Görünmez el: The phenomenon of the effective use of resources being ensured and social welfare increasing as a result of the behavior of individuals working only for their own interests.
Götürü vergi: Taxes paid at certain intervals and in a fixed amount, independent of income or wealth.
Güdümlü Proje Desteği: The support type given to special-quality model projects, directed toward providing support directly without applying the project proposal call method, with their subject and conditions determined under the leadership and guidance of the relevant Development Agency, in line with the priorities envisaged in the regional plan.
Gümrük Beyannamesi: The document filled in in accordance with customs legislation in exporting, and submitted to the customs administration after being approved by the relevant exporters' association.
Gün İçi Likidite İmkanı - GİL: The TL borrowing facility provided by the CBRT to banks, in order to meet the urgent TL funding needs arising during the day in the banking system and to eliminate the blockages that may occur in the payment system, during the day (between 09:00 and 15:00) to be repaid by the end of the day (until the EFT closes) — within its limits and collateral, in return for a commission (interest-free).
Haciz: In the event that the debtor does not pay its debt of its own will, the seizure by the state (by the enforcement office), at the creditor's request, of the debtor's assets and rights (in an amount sufficient to cover the debt). Public Offering: the sale of a company's shares to a large number of previously unknown investors through solicitation or announcement.
Hakkaniyet: Deciding, with limited resources, which products will be produced, how, and for whom, in a way that everyone receives an equal share or the share they deserve.
Hanehalkı: The fundamental economic unit in which various economic activities such as production, consumption, wealth accumulation and the transfer of wealth are carried out.
Harcanabilir gelir: The income that a country's citizens receive after income tax and can use for consumption or saving.
Hariçte İşleme Rejimi: The system involving the prior exporting of raw materials to be processed, their importation back into our country as products after being processed, and providing exemption from every kind of tax in this process. Target Market Analysis: the evaluation, quantitatively and qualitatively, of the market to be addressed. HES: the abbreviation of Hydroelectric Power Plant, a plant type converting the power of flowing water into electricity.
Hazine Bonosu: Debt securities with a maturity of less than one year issued by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance of the Republic of Türkiye.
Hedef Kitle: The group or community that the message intended to be conveyed in communication activities aims to reach.
Herfindahl-Hirschman Endeksi: Or in short HHI: the market concentration measure calculated by squaring and summing the market share percentages of all the firms in a market.
Hesaben Saklama: Refers to the holding of instruments in accounts in the electronic environment. For example, the instruments purchased from a Treasury auction can, as demanded physically by the participants (these instruments are printed by the CBRT), be transferred to the participants' accounts in the electronic environment against a receipt. Individuals too can have their instruments held in accounts against a receipt. The subsequent deposit of a physically held instrument into an account also brings the instrument into this form.
